Open Visual Studio .NET 2003 (tested on final beta but not release).

In the game, run File and New . Notice that TicTacToe is available.
Close the game and application, Copy <drive>:\Modular\Chess\bin\Debug\Chess.dll to <drive>:\Modular\GameDesktop\bin\Debug

Set Device name text field to something new and click OK .
Close the Settings form and click Start and then Programs .

In the Open path text field, type <name> of your computer on the network and click OK .

"Password:" text
Enter your network PC password
"Domain:" text
Enter the domain of your PC (which I believe is optional).
Click OK .
Select PC file share file in emulator
Select "Images" directory
Select "Edit\Select All"
Open the virtual keyboard and press CTRL+C.
Select the Device icon on Main Menu and select "Program Files\GamePPC".

Close the "File Explorer" Form and close the "Programs" Form.

Establish an ActiveSync connection.

The Compact Framework should download and install on device if not installed already
Corresponding game application and supporting DLLs should download to the correct \Program Files\<project name> directory on device
Application should start automatically. Exit the application manually on the device.
Open Windows Explorer on the desktop computer.
Copy all <drive>:\Modular\GameDesktop\bin\Debug subdirectories to Mobile Device's \Program Files\<project name> directory. This copies the resource DLLs and Images to device

Restart the application manually on the device.

title: Diffie-Hellman Keys
params: Both participants agree to the "Diffie-Hellman parameters," a prime number (P), and a base number (G).
Participant 1 sends its DIFFIE-HELLMAN public key to participant 2.
Participant 2 computes the secret encryption key by using the information contained in participant 1's public key.
Participant 2 sends participant 1 its DIFFIE-HELLMAN public key.
Participant 1 computes the secret encryption key by using the information contained in participant 2's public key.
Both participants now have the same encryption key, which can be used for encrypting and decrypting data.

Allocate memory for the key.
